title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
excerpt: Veteran actor Pete Edochie, famed for his role as Okonkwo, dies after a battle with prostate cancer.
body:
## A Beloved Icon Leaves the Stage
Pete Edochie, one of Africa’s most celebrated film stars, died in the early hours of Wednesday in Enugu, Nigeria, at the age of 79.  His family announced that the veteran actor succumbed to a prolonged battle with prostate cancer.  Known for his deep, resonant voice and commanding presence, Edochie became a household name across the continent, often embodying powerful traditional rulers, wealthy businessmen, and family patriarchs.

## From Broadcast Beginnings to International Fame
Edochie’s career began in 1967 as a broadcaster before he turned to acting.  He shot to prominence in 1987 when he starred as Okonkwo in a television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s classic novel *Things Fall Apart*.  The role earned him international recognition and cemented his status as one of Nigeria’s most respected actors.  The series portrayed the upheaval of an African community under British colonial rule and the spread of Christianity, showcasing Edochie’s ability to bring complex cultural narratives to life.

## A Pillar of Nollywood’s Rise
Over the decades, Edochie appeared in numerous films, including *Igodo*, *Rituals*, *Billionaire’s Club* and the 2018 romantic comedy *Lionheart*.  His contributions helped shape Nollywood into one of the world’s largest film industries.  In 2003, he received the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON), and later the Industry Merit Award at the Africa Magic Viewers Choice Awards.  In recent years, his memorable lines and facial expressions found new fans through viral social‑media memes.

## Tributes from Across the Continent
Fans, fellow actors, and officials quickly shared their condolences.  His son Leo posted a heartfelt Instagram message, praying for Edochie’s soul and strength for the family.  Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah called the loss “huge,” noting that Edochie introduced international audiences to Igbo traditions and inspired younger performers.  The Actors Guild of Nigeria president Abubakar Yakubu described him as a “father figure” whose influence will endure for generations.

## A Legacy That Lives On
Edochie is survived by his wife Josephine and six children, including Nollywood actors Yul and Linc Edochie.  Even as he faced health challenges—publicly speaking about difficulty walking and swelling during a 2023 visit to Ghana—he remained a beloved figure whose work continues to resonate.  His passing marks the end of an era, but his films, proverbs, and the cultural pride he championed will keep his spirit alive in the hearts of audiences across Africa and beyond.
